newsitem.title: UK: Cable&Wireless underlying interim profits up.
newsitem.headline: Cable&Wireless underlying interim profits up.

text.p: Britain's Cable & Wireless Plc on Wednesday said its first half pretax profits excluding exceptional items rose nine percent to 673 million pounds ($1.13 billion).
The results beat most analysts' expectations for underlying profits, which ranged from 650 to 668 million pounds.
C&W also raised its interim dividend to 3.4 pence per share from 3.08 pence in the year-ago period.

The interim results excluded an exceptional profit of 61 million pounds on the company's sale of part of its stake in AsiaSat, and a gain last year of 199 million pounds on the sale of its stake in Germany's Mannesmann Mobilfunk.
"We have delivered a strong competitive performance during the first half, and I remain confident about the outlook," chief executive Richard Brown said in a statement.

He added that operating margins rose to 25 percent in the six months ended September 30 compared to 23 percent, while cash flow from operations exceeded 1.0 billion pounds, an increase of 229 million pounds.
C&W shares were marked up four pence at 487 by 0815 GMT. ($1=.5970 Pound)
